heading: ## Dependency constraints
reason: No independently testable assertion at runtime: it governs how dependencies are PINNED (pyproject.toml plus uv.lock) and requires a propose-change cycle plus a minor bump to add one. The lock file is the artifact and a resolving install is the evidence; the propose-change requirement is process, enforced at review. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Forbidden patterns
reason: Mapped to the test witnessing the first and load-bearing forbidden pattern: no silent fallback may hide a transport error, so retry exhaustion MUST land at RefStatus.UNKNOWN rather than at a fabricated answer. Note this is the very clause livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.3 shows the ratified retry contract instructs consumers to VIOLATE. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Inherited from livespec
reason: No independently testable assertion: by construction it adds no rule of its own, adopting livespec-core's non-functional-requirements in full and pointing at this library's own file for the contributor-facing catalogue. Anything testable belongs to the upstream repo that owns the rule. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Process boundaries
reason: No independently testable assertion: every clause is an architectural NEGATIVE -- no threads, no asyncio, no subprocess pool, no filesystem mutation. A test can witness that the library did not do something on one path, which is not evidence it never does; the guarantee is upheld by review and by the absence of those imports, not by an assertion. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Provider constraints
reason: Mapped to the test witnessing the clause that providers MUST raise rather than swallow: a non-canonical github_url reaches the consumer as the provider's own domain exception. The future-provider bullets constrain modules that do not exist yet. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Public-surface constraints
reason: Enforced by CHECKS rather than by a pytest test: frozen/slotted/kw-only dataclasses and keyword-only functions are asserted by check-keyword-only-args and check-no-inheritance, and the inventory itself by check-all-declared. The one clause here that IS test-shaped, the kind-to-prefix lockstep, is exercised by tests/consumer/test_attention_lockstep.py and mapped from its own scenario heading. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Resolution-substrate constraints
reason: Mapped to the test witnessing the load-bearing clause: the walk MUST tolerate partial visibility, so an absent sibling_status_lookup yields UNKNOWN rather than an error or a guess. The no-cache/purity clause is an architectural negative with no positive observation to make. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Consumption shape
reason: No independently testable assertion at runtime: it fixes how consumers DECLARE the dependency (a uv git source, as a dev dependency or a runtime one). The declaration is exercised by installation itself -- CI resolving and importing the package is the evidence -- and nothing in the library observes it. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Module-level public surface
reason: Owned but NOT yet adjudicated. This heading still carries the li-univck Phase 3.3 seeding default rather than a per-heading disposition. `test: "TODO"` with a non-empty reason is a compliant terminal state for a non-scenarios.md heading, so this entry is not a gate failure; it is unfinished bookkeeping. livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2 decides, per heading, whether it names a real test or records the specific reason it carries no independently testable assertion. Re-pointed from livespec-runtime-nhs, whose scope was ownership and which is closed as satisfied; entries must not name a closed work-item.

heading: ## Resolution semantics
reason: Mapped to the consumer-tier resolution walk, which drives resolve_ref through the ratified per-variant return table. The sibling variants are exercised by the neighbouring tests in the same module, each already mapped from its own scenario heading. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Retry policy
reason: Mapped to the test that witnesses the whole ratified policy at once: three attempts consuming exactly TWO backoff sleeps, which is what pins the reserved-but-unused 4.0s constant as unused. Unit tier is permitted here -- the integration-tier rule binds scenarios.md only. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## System dependencies
reason: Mapped to the test that exercises the consumer-visible consequence this section ratifies: the runtime does NOT shell-detect `gh`, so its absence or failure surfaces as an exception that the retry layer collapses to RefStatus.UNKNOWN. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Versioning
reason: No independently testable assertion OF ITS OWN: this section delegates, stating that the semver bump rules and the pin-and-bump mechanism live in non-functional-requirements.md §"Versioning". The untested rule and its tracked gap are recorded on that heading, which points at livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.1. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## `.livespec.jsonc` `compat` block (consumer-facing)
reason: No independently testable assertion by THIS library: it constrains what a CONSUMER must declare in its own .livespec.jsonc. This repo cannot verify a rule whose subject lives in another repository -- the same reason v014 rejected the producer-emission-boundary alternative for attention-id validation. Enforcement belongs to whatever reads the consumer's config. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Boundary
reason: No independently testable assertion: meta-prose stating which invariants this FILE covers and which belong to contracts.md or constraints.md. It is the placement litmus, not a rule an implementation can violate. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Build and packaging
reason: No independently testable assertion at runtime: it fixes build configuration (hatchling backend, a single wheel from livespec_runtime/). The declarations live in pyproject.toml and are exercised by the build itself -- a failing build is the signal, and an importable installed package is the evidence CI already produces. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Inherited from livespec
reason: No independently testable assertion: by construction it restates no rule of its own, adopting livespec-core's non-functional-requirements in full and listing notable inherited rules for orientation only. Anything testable here belongs to the upstream repo that owns the rule. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Prose conventions
reason: No independently testable assertion about the library: it constrains how this SPEC's prose is written (version references prefixed with the owning project name). Violating it produces a misleading document, not misbehaving code. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Release flow
reason: No pytest test today, and the gap is TRACKED rather than dismissed: the section binds releases to release-please's manifest-mode config, but nothing asserts that the computed bump matches the ratified classification. That gap released 0.21.5 for a Major-classified change and is owned by livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.1; whatever closes it is the right mapping for this heading. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Repo layout
reason: Enforced by a CHECK rather than by a pytest test: the load-bearing clause -- that tests/ mirrors the livespec_runtime/ package layout -- is asserted by check-tests-mirror-pairing. The remaining bullets describe directory purposes, which carry no assertion. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Spec evolution
reason: No independently testable assertion: it describes this spec's own lifecycle and names compat.pinned as the authoritative consumed version. The lifecycle invariants are doctor's (see spec.md §'Lifecycle and evolution'); the pin is consumer configuration. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Task-runner discipline
reason: Enforced by CHECKS rather than by a pytest test: that `just` is the single canonical entry point, and that ruff/pyright/pytest are not invoked directly, is asserted by check-no-direct-tool-invocation and check-canonical-recipe-fidelity. A test asserting a check runs would be indirection, not coverage. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Test discipline
reason: Enforced by CHECKS rather than by a pytest test: 'every public symbol MUST have direct test coverage' is asserted by check-per-file-coverage and check-tests-mirror-pairing, and the scenario-tier rule this very registry implements is asserted by check-heading-coverage. The section governs the SUITE, so a test inside the suite cannot be its own witness. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Versioning
reason: No pytest test today, and the gap is TRACKED rather than dismissed: this section IS the ratified Major/Minor/Patch classification plus the pre-major provision, and nothing binds it to the bump release automation computes -- the defect that nearly shipped 0.21.5 for a Major-classified change. Owned by livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.1; whatever closes it is the right mapping for this heading. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Lifecycle and evolution
reason: Enforced by CHECKS rather than by a pytest test: it describes the livespec propose/critique/revise lifecycle, whose invariants are asserted by the doctor static registry via check-doctor-static (doctor-out-of-band-edits, doctor-version-contiguity, doctor-revision-to-proposed-change-pairing). No library behavior to exercise. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Public surface
reason: No independently testable assertion OF ITS OWN: this section delegates, naming contracts.md §'Module-level public surface' as the authoritative inventory. The testable content lives under that heading, which carries its own registry entry; duplicating a mapping here would make two entries move together silently. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Purpose
reason: No independently testable assertion: orientation prose stating what this library is and is not. Its one assertable claim -- that the package ships no slash commands, SKILL.md files or hooks -- is a repo-SHAPE fact, not runtime behavior, and is already declared in `.livespec.jsonc` `harnesses`, where both the claude and codex entries are recorded `exempt` with the reason 'livespec-runtime is a library; it ships no command/skill surface'. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Scope boundary
reason: No independently testable assertion: meta-prose delimiting which decisions this spec owns versus which are fixed upstream in livespec-core. It constrains the SPEC's contents, not the library's behavior. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.

heading: ## Terminology
reason: No independently testable assertion: a glossary. It adopts livespec-core's terms verbatim and adds library-local refinements; definitions carry no input/output an implementation could satisfy or violate. Adjudicated under livespec-runtime-mqsxsu.2.
